### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **1** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fabd25958f9908c51db18057ac3c4e73c4994edf` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bc0dd4845624790a495f8d8c7fd917bc67401ebb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.flow-record-read-and-decision-type-mismatch-refused.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts (the flow walk, `objectName = startObject ?? sweepObject`, `sweepsTypedObject`, `faultOutcomeOf`), packages/lint/src/validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts (`flow-time-relative-object-mismatch`), packages/spec/src/automation/time-relative-trigger.zod.ts (`object` required), packages/spec/src/automation/flow-trigger-kind.ts (`resolveFlowTriggerKind`), packages/triggers/trigger-schedule/src/time-relative-trigger.ts (`{ record: row }`), packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts (`SemanticMigration`), docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md (D3), packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas.ts (check b, exact-key registration), PR #30276's diff at `cfb602c4` and `.changeset/30026-time-relative-sweep-typing.md`, `.changeset/30283-time-relative-object-mismatch.md` at `54b491ad`

Inputs: card #30279 (body; comments 6650100066 triage, 6665805154 claim, 6667452302 os-dev-report), PR #30637 (body, 3-file list, net diff `origin/main...bc0dd484`, merge-base `25fea77a`), the head's check-runs. The rest of the diff (`.changeset/30279-time-relative-entry-surface.md`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/migrations.test.ts`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT; it is read here as evidence for ② and ④, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **No accept set moves — right.** The diff touches two string literals of one shipped `SemanticMigration` (`surface`, one `reason` sentence); `id`, `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria` are byte-identical on the diff (hunks at lines 10-15 and 25-33 only), the entry declares no `conversionIds` or `relevance` before or after, and it stays a semantic entry of major 18 (the `entries/semantic/18.` path the generator classifies by; `SemanticMigration` itself has no `kind` field, so the PR body's "kind" can only mean that). No gate reads the entry's prose as a machine fact: `build-schemas.ts` check (b) registers a retirement by EXACT key in `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` (the leaf-vs-`surface` match was retired at #4659), and `SemanticRelevance` is "never a match against the prose of `surface`" (`types.ts`). So no author-time verdict, publish-door verdict or chain result changes.
- **Public surface — right.** `@objectstack/spec` publishes the entry through the generated registry, `os migrate meta`, `spec-changes.json` and the upgrade guide; what every one of them shows moves by exactly these two strings. The registry (`packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts`) is gitignored and rebuilt on install and build, so no tracked generated artifact carries the text; `git grep` of the FROM phrase on `origin/main` hits only the entry itself and the #30026 changeset's prose. The dev's `check:generated` reading (14 artifacts, nothing regenerated) agrees with the tree.
- **The text now describes the gate — right.** `validate-expressions.ts` 2736-2740: `objectName = startObject ?? sweepObject`, with `sweepObject` read from `config.timeRelative.object` on a `time_relative` flow; 2857-2861: `sweepsTypedObject: sweepObject !== undefined && sweepObject === objectName`; `faultOutcomeOf` 1353-1355 declares `run-fails` for `time_relative` only under `sweepsTypedObject`. That is exactly "typed against that object when the start node names no objectName and against the start node's objectName when that is the swept object": the two cases where `sweepObject === objectName` are `startObject === undefined` and `startObject === sweepObject`. The `object` key is required in `TimeRelativeTriggerSchema` (`.string().regex(MACHINE_NAME)`, no `.optional()`), so "sweeping config.timeRelative.object" names the one object every sweep has. `time-relative-trigger.ts:657` launches each run with `{ record: row }`, the swept row, as the reason says.
- **Tracker ids in runtime strings — none.** The new `surface` and `reason` text carries no `#NNNN`; the only ids in the PR are in the changeset body and the PR body, which do not ship as runtime strings.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/30279-time-relative-entry-surface.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` as line-initial declarations in the body; the PR body carries the same two lines. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: a bug fix in a released package takes `patch`, never none; `Metadata-protocol: none` is right (no key, accepted value or meaning an author writes changes; what moves is explanatory text); `Clause-②: no` is right (no accept-set move at any gate, per ①). No `!` in the PR title, no BREAKING banner, no ADR-0087 marker: none is owed on a non-breaking changeset, and `check:adr-0087-registration` ("this PR adds no declared-breaking changeset") agrees. The changeset body states the FROM phrase and that id, kind, replacement and acceptance criteria are unchanged, which is what the diff publishes. **Matches.**
- Clause-② line: `no`. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev note / out_of_scope_findings — "Any other flow keeps a warning" left as is, now that `flow-time-relative-object-mismatch` refuses a time-relative start whose `objectName` is not `timeRelative.object`.** Answered: the sentence stays true of the verdict this entry governs, and the entry is the right place for no more. The sentence is about the type-mismatch verdict: on a sweep of another object the expression gate serves `type-mismatch-run-may-fail` as a warning (`faultOutcomeOf` returns `undefined`, 1353-1356) plus the #30026 explanatory warning at `config.objectName` (3283-3300), and nothing in the diff or on `main` turns that into a refusal. The refusal of such a start is a different rule with its own id, grade (`severity: 'error'`, `validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts:741`), `os explain` text, and a changeset whose ADR-0087 disposition (`54b491ad`, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`) states in writing that this entry "prescribes a rewrite of a condition, not of the start node" and that no ledger entry covers the start-node combination. An entry sentence saying the flow is refused for another reason would be an erratum about a rule it does not govern. Holds; no finding.
- **`open_questions`: []** — nothing to answer.
- **PR Acceptance notes, "a start that names another object keeps the warning"** — confirmed against `faultOutcomeOf` (above).
- **PR Acceptance notes, "no tracker id in a runtime string"** — confirmed by reading the two strings on the head.
- **Dev's whole-package `pnpm test` NOT MEASURED locally (verify-lock queue timeout)** — declared narrowing to `src/migrations/` (the suite that reads the entry); CI `Test Core` covers the package. The head's check-runs, read after every one completed: 64 runs, 55 `success`, 9 `skipped` (UI Published Artifacts, Dogfood Verify CLI, Build Docs, the dogfood shard matrix, Temporal Conformance, Packed-tarball smoke, the schedule gate, Lint UI, all opt-in or path-gated), 0 `failure`; `Test Core` 8/8 shards, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` and `Lint · docs & code guards` among the successes. Closed by the gate.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.flow-record-read-and-decision-type-mismatch-refused.ts`, against ADR-0087 D3, `SemanticMigration` and the gate it describes:

- **Against the gate (no more, no less).** Each clause of the new `surface` tail and `reason` sentence maps to one line of `validate-expressions.ts`: "sweeping config.timeRelative.object" is `sweepObject` (2739); "typed against that object when the start node names no objectName" is `startObject ?? sweepObject` with `startObject === undefined` (2740); "against the start node's objectName when that is the swept object" is `sweepObject === objectName` with `startObject` set (2860); "get the same refusal" is `run-fails` (1353-1355) under the `-run-fails` code (1334). The reason's history clause is right on both arms: "where 18.3.0 warned on a sweep of the start node's objectName" is the shipped text's own claim, and "where a start that names no objectName got no verdict at all" is what the #30026 changeset's Before paragraph records (no type verdict at all; PR #30276 made `sweepsTypedObject` require `sweepObject !== undefined` instead of `typeof sweep.object !== 'string'`). Nothing in the text claims more than the gate does: it does not say a sweep of another object is refused by this verdict, and it does not say such a flow publishes. Holds.
- **A start that names no `objectName`: `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria` still hold.** The replacement (the text's length via `size(record.name)`, a number field for a value, `double(...)` on numeric text, `record.active == true` for a boolean) rewrites the condition, which is the same condition whichever object it is typed against. The acceptance criteria name "a record-triggered or time-relative flow's condition, decision branch or record.FIELD read" and the `type-mismatch-run-fails` code: a flow whose start names no `objectName` is a time-relative flow, gets that code (1334), and publishes through `publish-drafts` once the condition compares like with like; the readiness rule does not fire on it (`namedObject !== undefined` is false, `validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts:735`). The "create on POST /api/v1/data/OBJECT that should start the flow" sentence is the record-triggered arm's and was already there. Holds.
- **Against ADR-0087 D3 and `SemanticMigration`.** D3's structured TODO is "(surface, reason, acceptance criteria)", the reason being the one load-bearing prose field; the entry keeps all four fields and the stable kebab-case `id`. The surface head (`automation.Flow of ...`) is unchanged, so the ' / '-split clause vocabulary the check-mode fixture reads (`minRegisteredMajorForLeaf`) sees the same clauses. The entry stays on major 18 in the semantic registry. Holds.
- **Trigger-kind edge.** A start carrying a `record-*` `triggerType` and a `timeRelative` descriptor resolves to `record_change` first (`flow-trigger-kind.ts`), so it is covered by the entry's record-triggered arm and never by the time-relative one; the readiness rule's `!isArrayRecordTriggered` exemption agrees. The text needs no clause for it.
- **should-fix — `packages/spec/src/migrations/migrations.test.ts:814`.** The new pin matches only `/sweeping config\.timeRelative\.object/`. The correction's substance is the two typing clauses that follow ("typed against that object when the start node names no objectName and against the start node's objectName when that is the swept object"); a regression that keeps the first six words and drops the clauses passes this pin, and the ablation the dev ran mutates the whole tail at once, so it does not show the gap. One more `toMatch` on `names no objectName` (or on the `reason` sentence) closes it. Not a FAIL: the entry text on the head is right, the pin is a guard on a future edit.

No must-fix.
